A.summary: Admitted domain (accessibility, non-turns, no obstacles/observers, single-file local .geojson, roles network/origins/destinations) is internally consistent and conservatively subset relative to the design.

findings.claim: RunAccessibility dispatches non-turns rows to AccessibilityWElevation only (UNA.py:338-379), so admitting 'accessibility + non-turns' pins exactly one engine; obstacles are loaded only when obstacle_points_file is set (UNA.py:333-334) and observers are never touched by RunAccessibility.

Geojson-only v1 admission is evidence-backed: tests/cache/invalidation/conftest.py builds network/origins/destinations/obstacles as .geojson exclusively (to_file driver='GeoJSON'); .feather/.parquet appear in tests/cache only as OUTPUT formats (test_output_only_changes_reuse.py). The buffer reader branch for geojson (Topology.py:78) is the one the parity pin exercises (test_warm_cold_off_artifacts_bitwise_equal, test_parity_safety_engagement.py:39).

Nothing needlessly excluded: the design itself permits a tested-only subset ('First admit single-file .geojson/.feather/.parquet only where tested', design line 82); obstacle exclusion is justified because the obstacle arc-penalty state (obstacle_arc_penalty_AB/BA/node_penalty, Topology.py:144-155) and AddObstacles' own gate set (Topology.py:669-703) are outside the three prepared payloads and have no store/restore path today.

Elevation handling is sound: z is extracted unconditionally in BuildTopology (Topology.py:1604-1608), stored (351) and restored (395), while settings.elevation gates only engine USE (AccessibilityWElevation.py:832) — elevation correctly stays out of preparation identity.

B.summary: Closure completeness verified against the actual producers. Every producer-read input is inside the proposed keys; every excluded input is genuinely unread. Two residual closure gaps found (role/label, extension) plus one unproven invariance (num_threads).

findings.claim: Topology closure complete: AddNetwork reads source bytes (208), network_weight_column (217, 283-286), network_precision (315), network_load_nodes (305-310); all three params are in the proposed key (contract identity_law.topology == Topology.py:233-244). network_weight_default is assigned at 218 and never read again in the method body — its exclusion is correct.

Snap closure: BuildAccessPoints reads source bytes, cost_attribute (1072-1075), uid_attribute (1105), and the parent network state (geometry/sindex/weights/start_nodes/end_nodes, 1128-1179) — covered by file_sha256 + parent_network_stage chaining (Topology.py:1019-1030). default_cost is never consumed by the arithmetic (only 'Count' sentinel, column-present, and fallback branches) but IS keyed (1024) — over-keying, permitted by the design.

Excluded inputs verified unread: grep over Topology.py:195-1200 finds zero search_radius/gravity_beta/elevation references in the preparation paths; BuildTurnPenalties is commented out (Topology.py:317); BuildTopology itself reads only self.geometry/self.weights/precision/discard flag (Topology.py:1503-1615, no settings or num_threads reads).

FINDING B-1 (counterexample): the snap-stage key uses stage id 'una:snap:v1' for ALL roles (Topology.py:1019) with no role/label component, while the producing code embeds the role label into stored replay text (nan_warning 1083-1090, fallback_warning 1094-1100 -> log_extras 478-479). Two rows (or two roles in one row) with identical bytes + identical cost/default/uid params + same network collide on one entry and the second consumer replays the FIRST role's label ('Origins' vs 'Destinations') where the current path logs its own. Legal admitted input: origins_file == destinations_file. The contract's own stage_inventory names role-split stages ('una:snap:v1[origins]') which does NOT match the code its consistency determination says it must serve. This fixes the key schema and must be resolved before implementation.
findings.status: REFUTED as written / must be resolved

findings.claim: FINDING B-2: design layer 1 includes format/extension in SourceSnapshot identity, but the contract's closure omits extension. Within geojson-only v1 every non-feather/parquet extension takes the identical reader branch (Topology.py:78) so a renamed file cannot decode differently, and a bytes-identical file with a .feather/.parquet extension fails loudly (wrong reader), never silently. Low risk, but either add extension to the closure or record this argument.

FINDING B-3: topology.num_threads shapes BuildAccessPoints chunking (1116: max_workers = min(self.num_threads, len(weights))) and is NOT in the snap key. Bit-safety holds by construction (ordered array_split -> ordered concatenate at 1134/1139/1157/1165-1169, elementwise shapely ops), but no test pins bit-equality across num_threads values.

C.summary: Every error gate in audit section 2 verified line-exact against the code, in the claimed order. The fallback law is sound; the hit path's skip of inner re-validation is safe ONLY via the content-identity argument (deterministic producer + complete closure + env in key), which holds except where finding B-1 breaks log identity.

findings.claim: AddNetwork order: isfile FileNotFoundError (210-211) -> has_clusters reset (215) -> geometry-type ValueError with null-geometry naming (255-271) -> CRS-None warning v1 / CRS-set log v2 (273-276) -> 'Network added from source' v1 (278) -> weight NaN/non-positive guard with logged warning (291-301). Matches audit exactly.

BuildAccessPoints order: geometry gate (1041-1047) BEFORE CRS gates (1048-1058) BEFORE weight resolution ('Count' 1072-1073; column NaN warning 1074-1092; missing-column fallback 1093-1104) BEFORE uid (1105). So wrong-geometry + bad-CRS together raises the geometry error; NaN-weight vs geometry gate: geometry wins. Matches audit exactly.

Missing file vs missing column: FileNotFoundError at the Add* isfile gate (552, 571) precedes any decode; a missing weight column is a logged fallback inside BuildAccessPoints, never an error. Both preserved on the miss/owner path.

Hit-path error safety: a content-derived failure implies no entry exists for that key (produce raised before put_arrays), so a hit cannot suppress an error the current path would raise, PROVIDED the closure is complete (see B-1 for the one log-text exception). settings.Validation() (UNA.py:322) and per-role isfile gates run before any session consult and are outside the prepared block.

Contract refusal taxonomy (session absent, stage not admitted, format, payload not representable, store failure, NO_FIT, owner failure) covers every observed refusal class; the existing store refuses non-representable payloads as skip-not-error (stages.py:124-138, 58-61) and mixed-dimension WKB is a skip at Topology.py:96-97/339-341 with identity still recorded (340).

D.summary: Restore inventory is complete for every consumer I could reach (engine init, CSR build, Centrality re-read, exports, ODM, composite, state-bundle pickle). One log-replay gap found; one audit description error found.

findings.claim: Engine init reads exactly: network start_nodes/end_nodes/weights/node_points/z (AccessibilityWElevation.py:635-644), get_obstacle_arc_penalties (681 -> (None,None) when no obstacles, Topology.py:786-788, defensive .copy()), origins edge_start_node/edge_end_node/weight_to_start/weight_to_end (693-696), destinations node_weight/edge_start/end/weight_to_start/weight_to_end (699-703), get_partial_edge_corrections (719, 732), logger (796). All are in the stored/restored set (Topology.py:342-356, 389-399, 464-495, 507-526).

Centrality re-reads topology.destinations.node_weight (901) - restored. Exports read origins.geometry (Base.py:155-156), net.geometry.crs (297, 347, 480), observer/obstacle uid+geometry (380, 402 - outside v1 domain), ODM uids (237-238, 481) - all restored. Composite reads net.node_points + net.geometry.crs (UNA.py:_build_composite_nodes_gdf) and re-reads input FILES via gpd.read_file(join_path) rather than prepared state - parity trivial.

FINDING D-1: the produce path logs 'CRS set to {self.crs}.' at v=2 (Topology.py:276); _restore_network_from_cache (374-433) replays no_crs, edge count, weight warning, empty-removed, topology counts, edge_list_dict and the hit announcement but NOT the CRS-set line. Warm log streams at verbosity>=2 diverge from cold by this line (plus the accepted hit-announcement line). Audit section 10's inventory omits it from BOTH lists, so the audit's own 'content-derived v<=2 lines replayed' law is violated by its own inventory.

FINDING D-2 (audit error): audit section 7.2 describes line 179 as reading 'topology.origins.geometry.crs'; it actually reads 'self.topology.origins.crs if hasattr(self.topology.origins, 'crs') else None' and AccessPoints has NO crs attribute anywhere (class def Topology.py:2449-2485), so this yields None on BOTH current and restored paths. Results-GDF CRS parity flows from results_data['geometry'] (Base.py:155-156), not this kwarg. Conclusion unaffected; description wrong.

Freshness/aliasing: get_arrays decodes fresh arrays per call (stages.py:69-75, docstring 18-23); restore attaches them to a fresh AccessPoints/logger-local object; clasters_byId={} fresh via __init__; has_clusters reset before any hit return (215, 560, 576); network lengths-not-filtered-by-empty-removal quirk is stored/restored verbatim (281 vs BuildTopology filtering only weights) - preserved, not fixed, per design line 106.

State-bundle pickling surface (worker.py:423-431 packs topology+engine) is satisfied by the restore set; the only non-picklable member, edge_sindex, is rebuilt at restore (400-403), matching the batch rehydration contract.

E.summary: Seam census independently re-verified; the contract's claim is both necessary and sufficient.

findings.claim: cache_options appears at exactly six src sites: Topology.py:184 (init None), 192 (per-Add* refresh via _apply_stage_cache_policy 188-193), 226 and 1013 (Add* preparation resolution), AccessibilityWElevation.py:930-931 and Accessibility.py:841-842 (engine RESULT stage). No other reader exists.

Injecting the session's store through cache_options would therefore (a) be clobbered by the next Add*'s policy refresh AND (b) enable the una:awe:o_access:v1 results stage (930-938) for every subsequent row - the contract's stated reason for a separate resolver attribute is correct.

Two preparation resolution sites only: AddObstacles/AddObservers carry no separate stage-cache resolution - they read snapshots directly and route through BuildAccessPoints (Topology.py:660-705, 583-614), so a resolver at 226 and 1013 covers every preparation stage including refused-domain calls; v1 refusals for turns/obstacles/flow must be evaluated at the hook with row settings in hand.

Under cache-off + prepared session, restored _stage_key values are consumed only by the snap chaining gate (1016, 1021) and the engine key computation (854-856), which is then unused because cache.enabled is False (932) - no observable artifact change. The cohort wrapper (UNA.py:392-397) reads only _cohort_session, not cache state.

Leak check: the state bundle pickles topology+engine after the cohort detach point (worker.py:401-431); the prepared session must detach there too (contract says so). RowResult carries counters only (cohort precedent 199-235). The stage_cache_for global registry (stages.py:204-231) is keyed by CacheOptions tuples and never sees the session unless the session deliberately routes through it.

F.summary: arrays_once satisfies the design's state machine for ABSENT/BUILDING/COMPLETE with bounded fallback; LEASED is session-level work; memory laws match the existing code; the registry concern is real.

findings.claim: produce() AND commit run inside the per-key flight (stages.py:173-177); an owner exception leaves no commit and releases the lock via the context manager; a loser that acquires after a failed owner yields True (singleflight yields True when 'lock acquired and no generation committed yet', store.py:651-655) -> re-elect; dead holders are stolen via pid liveness (store.py:662-663); bounded paths: spins>=3 local compute (180-184), wait_timeout_s=60 TimeoutError local compute (185-187). No partial acceptance: put is atomic (tmp + os.link O_EXCL) and reads verify checksums on_read by default (store.py:18-23, 397-412) with quarantine+miss, never a raise to the caller.

LEASED has no machinery in StageCache - it must be built at session level for residency; the existing precedent is TraceResidency's ResidentLease acquire/release/close (trace_residency.py:105-130, 311, 357), which the contract could cite as the reuse surface instead of implying arrays_once covers it.
findings.status: CONFIRMED (gap is acknowledged implicitly, precedent uncited)

findings.claim: Memory law matches existing code: per_worker_residency_cap is max(64 MiB, allowance // workers) (cohort.py:102-103); NO_FIT-as-refusal is a session-level admission wrapper around produce(), which arrays_once does not provide - implementation obligation, consistent with design lines 116-118.

Registry-bound concern is REAL: _PROCESS_STORES (cohort.py:158-168) is a per-root dict with insertion only, no eviction and no run-end close; a long-lived process serving multiple roots grows it without bound. The contract correctly refuses to add a second such registry.

Session-store verification policy is NOT pinned in the contract; the store default is on_read and the campaign law says verification on_read is not downgradable. The contract must pin it (on_read or always) for the session-constructed ContentStore.

G.summary: The per-row snapshot-read law closes the TOCTOU class as claimed; no hole found.

findings.claim: Every row reads and hashes its OWN snapshot before any cache consult (Topology.py:232 network, 1017-1018 snap), and the owner decodes THOSE SAME bytes (250-252, 1036-1038). A waiter's key is computed from its own bytes; hash equality with the owner's key is the only trust, and sha256 collision is out of scope. A mid-run mutation produces a different digest -> a different key -> the mutating row recomputes from its own bytes with its own content-derived warnings.

'Waiters serve bytes they never observed' is impossible in this structure: the flight commits under a key the waiter itself derived; the owner's decode input is its own snapshot, whose digest is that key. The ABA case (file returns to earlier bytes) correctly hits the earlier identity's payload - the row genuinely observed those bytes.

Snapshot bytes are fully in-memory (open(rb).read(), Topology.py:55-61) - bounded by input size; the design's 'bounded/spooled with the copy charged' requires the session's admission reservation to count them (contract memory_law includes build scratch). AddObstacles' snapshot pass-through (674-680, review MINOR-3 precedent) is outside v1.

H.summary: Five mandated scenarios plus one adversarial addition. Four produce current-path behavior; two findings (B-1 log-label collision; D-1 CRS log line) are real divergences.

scenarios.scenario: Two rows, identical network bytes, different network_precision, same run.
scenarios.outcome: CORRECT: precision is in the topology closure (Topology.py:237) -> distinct keys -> two builds, two snaps chains; single-flight is per-key so neither poisons the other. Residency governs the two resident payloads. Contract handles it as written.

scenarios.scenario: Origins file gains a NaN weight between row 3 and row 17.
scenarios.outcome: CORRECT: row 17's own isfile gate + snapshot read yield a different file_sha256 -> miss -> row 17 decodes its OWN bytes, emits its OWN NaN warning (1074-1092) and stores under the new key - identical class/order/text to the current path. Row 3's served payload matches what row 3's current path produced. Win is lost for the mutated identity only, which is correct.

scenarios.scenario: Turn-enabled row arrives while a session is attached.
scenarios.outcome: SOUND BY CONTRACT: Add* sites run before the turns dispatch (UNA.py:324-326 vs 338), so the hook must refuse turns-stages from row settings; refusal taxonomy covers it ('stage not admitted'); the cohort wrapper independently never arms for turns (393, C31-NOTE-3). Needs an explicit P02I test (refusal counted + byte-identical artifacts).

scenarios.scenario: Owner worker dies mid-build while 3 workers wait.
scenarios.outcome: SOUND: SIGKILL -> file lock stolen via pid liveness (store.py:662-663); a waiter acquires, sees no committed generation, yields True and produces (re-elect). Exception death -> context manager releases the lock uncommitted, same result. Late duplicate publish can only emit an identical generation (key closure pins all inputs). Wait timeout (60s) or 3 unproductive spins degrade to local compute - duplicated work, never wrong bits; the timed-out waiter's local compute is today's memory class. Contract's loser_path determination is accurate.

scenarios.scenario: Store payload corrupted between production and a later row's hit.
scenarios.outcome: SOUND at the machinery level: on_read verification quarantines + reports the entry as a miss (store.py:18-23, 397-412, 461-499); arrays_once re-enters the flight and rebuilds. Contract requires this to surface as a distinct corruption_rebuild counter (today StageCache stats do not distinguish it) - implementation obligation, consistent with design line 114. Session-store verification mode must be pinned (finding F-5).

scenarios.scenario: REVIEWER-ADDED: origins_file == destinations_file (identical bytes), same cost/default/uid params, weight column present with NaN (or configured column missing).
scenarios.outcome: FINDING: both roles derive the SAME snap key (Topology.py:1019 - no role/label in closure). The first role produces and stores log_extras carrying ITS label ('Origins weight column ... NaN', 1083-1090; fallback text likewise, 1094-1100); the second role hits and replays the wrong role's label where the current path logs 'Destinations ...'. Artifacts stay bitwise-equal (arrays identical); the LOG STREAM diverges, violating the logs-identical law for a legal admitted input. Latent today in CACHE_GRAPH (both roles share the store); amplified by a run-scoped session where both roles are always in one run. Not reachable in the frozen 32-row cohort (distinct role files), but the parity law is domain-wide. Fix is a design-time choice: add role/label to the closure (safe: run-scoped store, no cross-route key compat needed) or store label-free replay text and re-label at restore.

document_errors.error: Names stages 'una:snap:v1[origins]' and 'una:snap:v1[destinations]' as distinct prepared stages, but the actual key at Topology.py:1019 uses stage id 'una:snap:v1' for all roles (metadata 'stage': 'una:snap:v1' at Topology.py:472) with no role component; resolved_determinations.cohort_stage_key_consistency simultaneously requires serving 'the SAME key ... the CACHE_GRAPH store path would'. The two statements cannot both be literal. Resolve per finding B-1/H6.

Claims the C30 cohort TRACE keys chain on stage-key identity via the engine's _stage_key reads. REFUTED: the cohort TraceID hashes CSR array bytes plus fixed semantics strings (_trace_access_scratch.py:169-218) and no code in batch/cohort.py or the trace modules reads _stage_key. The _stage_key consumers are the snap chaining gate (Topology.py:1016, 1021) and the CACHE_GRAPH engine/result keys (AccessibilityWElevation.py:854-856, Accessibility.py:770-772). Conclusion (set the same _stage_key) survives for CACHE_GRAPH consistency; the stated cohort coupling is wrong.

Describes Base.py:179 as reading 'topology.origins.geometry.crs'; it reads 'self.topology.origins.crs' under hasattr, and AccessPoints has no crs attribute (Topology.py:2449-2485), so the expression is None on both current and restored paths. Results CRS parity comes from results_data['geometry'] (Base.py:155-156).

Log replay inventory omits the produce-path v=2 line 'CRS set to {crs}.' (Topology.py:276), which _restore_network_from_cache (374-433) does not replay - so the section's own inventory contradicts the stated v<=2 replay law.

Says default_cost is 'NOT read in stages 1-3'; it IS read (Topology.py:546, 567 from settings.default_cost), passed into BuildAccessPoints, and keyed (1024) - it is unconsumed by the arithmetic. The contract's closure (which includes default_cost as an over-key) is correct; the audit's phrasing is not.

verified_correct: cache_options census exact (contract census_note): Topology.py:184, 192, 226, 1013; AccessibilityWElevation.py:930-931; Accessibility.py:841-842 - no other src reader.

All audit section 2 gate lines verified line-exact and in order (AddNetwork 210-211/255-271/273-276/291-301; BuildAccessPoints 1041-1047/1048-1053/1054-1058/1072-1073/1074-1092/1093-1104/1105; AddObstacles 669-672/681-685/687-692/693-703).
'19 tests' in test_dependency_mutations_miss.py is correct as pytest items: 11 functions + 1 parametrized x8 = 19 (grep counts 12 functions).
conftest geojson-only inputs confirmed (network/origins/destinations/obstacles .geojson; feather/parquet appear only as output flags in tests/cache).

cited parity tests exist at the cited lines: test_parity_safety_engagement.py:39 (warm/cold bitwise), :55 (restored crs), :74 (mutation cannot poison), :111 (same bytes new mtime), :127 (same bytes different path); test_hit_payloads_are_fresh_copies at tests/cache/store/test_roundtrip_warmcold.py:36.

arrays_once mechanics as cited: produce+commit in flight (stages.py:173-177), spins>=3 fallback (180-184), TimeoutError fallback (185-187), StageProduced MAJOR-1 law (89-99); singleflight pid-liveness steal and wait_timeout_s=60 (store.py:649-673).
per_worker_residency_cap = max(64 MiB, allowance // workers) (cohort.py:102-103) and the floor-binds sum exception; _PROCESS_STORES unbounded (158-168).
UNA.RunAccessibility order (UNA.py:316-407), cohort wrapper non-turns clause (392-397), worker attach/detach and state-bundle region (worker.py:347-431).
Store corruption law: on_read verification default, quarantine + miss, never a raise to the caller (store.py:18-23, 337-412, 461-499).

identity helpers as cited: stage_key (identity.py:135-140), file_digest (145-147), arrays_digest (150-164), geometry_env (186-209); network._stage_key/AccessPoints._stage_key class defaults None (Topology.py:1510, 2462).

blocking_findings.finding: Snap-stage role/label closure ambiguity (B-1/H6). The contract must state, before implementation, whether the P02 snap-stage key adds a role/label component to the CACHE_GRAPH-identical closure, or whether replay text is stored label-free and re-labeled per restore. As written, the contract's stage_inventory (role-split ids) contradicts its cohort_stage_key_consistency determination (serve the CACHE_GRAPH-identical 'una:snap:v1' key), and the CACHE_GRAPH-identical choice replays one role's label inside another role's log stream for the legal input origins_file == destinations_file. This is a key-schema decision that cannot be deferred to implementation-time evidence.
blocking_findings.why_blocking: Identity schema is the contract's core deliverable; both readings cannot be implemented, and one of them violates the logs-identical law on the admitted domain.

non_blocking_findings.finding: 'CRS set to {crs}.' v=2 line (Topology.py:276) is not replayed by _restore_network_from_cache; warm log streams diverge from cold at verbosity>=2 (inherited from CACHE_GRAPH). Replay it (the restored CRS object exists at that point) or enumerate the divergence as accepted at P02I.
Session-store verification policy unpinned; pin to on_read (or always) so the campaign's verification-on-read law is not downgradable by construction options.

Extension/format absent from the closure although design layer 1 includes it; geojson-only v1 is safe by reader-branch identity (Topology.py:78), but adding the extension to the closure is cheap and design-conformant before formats widen.
num_threads invariance of snap bits is argued by construction (ordered chunk map + concatenate, elementwise ops) but unproven; either pin it with a test or add num_threads to the closure.

LEASED has no machinery in StageCache; the session must build lease/residency accounting. TraceResidency (trace_residency.py:105-130, 311-357) is the existing lease precedent and should be cited as the reuse surface (design's 'reuse existing primitives').

v=3 snap log lines ('There are N points in M chunks', 'Nearest edge is found', 'Done') are not replayed on hits - accepted under the v<=2 law, but record it as an explicit accepted divergence for verbosity-3 runs.

A waiter that times out (60s) or exhausts spins computes locally, so under extreme skew up to W duplicate builds of one identity can run concurrently - correct bits, original-path memory class, but the engagement assert 'builds == distinct identities' must be measured at completion, not assumed mid-flight.
_PROCESS_STORES (cohort.py:158-168) is confirmed unbounded; out of P02 scope but worth an owner note since the prepared session is being held to the bound its predecessor lacks.

p02i_required_evidence: Public-surface bitwise parity: prepared-session warm/cold vs session-less cold on RunBatch (not just the CACHE_GRAPH entry point), on the frozen 32-row cohort shape AND on the invalidation-suite workload class (which includes elevation).

Log-stream parity defined and measured: verbosity 1 and 2 warm-vs-cold streams compared; either byte-identical (requires NF-1 replay) or an enumerated accepted-divergence list committed in the receipt; v3 divergence documented (NF-6).
Cross-role collision test (BF-1): origins_file == destinations_file with a NaN-bearing or missing weight column; both roles' log streams must equal the serial path's.

Engagement asserts with distinct counters: cold_build == number of distinct admitted identities per run; verified_hit, contention_wait (singleflight_lost), corruption_rebuild, refusal counts all observed nonzero in at least one fault-injection test each; zero refusals on the clean cohort.

Invalidation on the SESSION path (not inherited citations): changed bytes with unchanged size/mtime; mixed network_precision rows in one run; mid-run input mutation; uid dtype outside ifubU; mixed-dimension WKB; stale manifest / corrupted payload -> quarantine + rebuild counted as corruption_rebuild.
Owner-death test: kill -9 the owner mid-build with >=2 waiters; assert exactly one rebuild, no partial acceptance, waiters' artifacts bitwise-equal to serial.
Turns row with session attached: refusal counted, byte-identical artifacts/logs vs session-less current path, and no snap/topology entry created for the refused row.

Memory law: NO_FIT refusal observed and counted, row falls back bitwise; floor-bound cap unit pins reused; admission reservation includes snapshot bytes + build scratch + retained payload + decoded copies.
Detach law: assert the prepared session attribute is absent from the state-bundle pickle and RowResult for every row (no session-owned object survives transport).
Mutation isolation on the public surface: two rows sharing one identity in one worker; mutate row N's restored arrays/geometry; row N+1 and the store unaffected (freshness law on RunBatch).
num_threads bit-equality pin for the snap stage (NF-4), or closure inclusion.

Measurement of per-row snapshot re-read + hash cost netted inside the timed window (contract open question 1) - no off-clock setup; plus increment B/C interaction evidence: one decode per identity per run measured under B-then-C (contract open question 2).
disposition: The narrow initial domain and its failure-order law are sound to implement against: every admitted producer input is inside the proposed closure, every excluded setting is verifiably unread by the producers, the audit's error-gate inventory matches the code line-for-line, the restore set covers every consumer I could reach (engine init, CSR, Centrality, exports, ODM, composite, state-bundle pickle), the single-flight primitive genuinely provides owner-failure re-election with no partial acceptance, and the per-row snapshot law closes the TOCTOU class. The seam analysis is exactly right - the cache_options census admits no third path, so a separate resolver at Topology.py:226/1013 is both necessary and sufficient. One contract decision is blocking: the snap-stage closure must either add the role/label or store label-free replay text, because the contract currently asserts two incompatible key schemas and one of them replays the wrong role's warning label for the legal input origins_file == destinations_file (a logs-law violation, not a bits violation, and unreachable in the frozen cohort - hence fixable now at zero qualification cost). The inherited CACHE_GRAPH log gap ('CRS set to ...' not replayed) must be closed or explicitly accepted at P02I. I would reject the implementation if: any producer-read input is found outside the shipped keys, a hit skips a row's isfile/Validation gates, any refusal mutates observable state before falling back, warm artifacts or admitted-domain log streams diverge from the serial path beyond an enumerated accepted set, prepared state leaks into cache_options, the state bundle, or another row's objects, or the benefit is claimed without the counted cold_build/verified_hit/refusal evidence on the public surface.
